title: The Water King: The Bargain
subtitle: A promise made over a bridge — and a father who must pay with his son

help.excerpt: Vasilissa the Wise opened her window and asked: "What are you crying for, Prince?" "How can I help crying? Your father has ordered me to plant a garden in one night!" "That's nothing! lie down and sleep: the morning is wiser than the evening." She made him go to sleep, but she herself went out on the steps, called and whistled with a mighty whistle. From every side there ran together gardeners of all sorts, and they planted a garden green, and in the garden birds sang, on the trees flowers blossomed, from the boughs hung ripe apples and pears. Early in the morning Vasilissa the Wise awoke the Prince: "Get up, Prince! the garden is ready: Papa is coming to see it."

narrativeBlocks.title: Thirst at the bridge
narrativeBlocks.body: A merchant crossing a bridge stops to drink — and a hand from the water seizes him. The Water King demands the thing he loves most at home — or the thing he does not know he has.

narrativeBlocks.title: The fatal unknowing
narrativeBlocks.body: The merchant promises 'whatever is at home that I don't know about' — the classic trap. While he was away, his wife bore him a son: the bargain binds the child he has never seen.

narrativeBlocks.title: The son goes to pay
narrativeBlocks.body: Years later the debt is called. The boy — Ivan — must go to the Water King's underwater palace. He does not drown: in these tales the underwater world is simply another kingdom.

narrativeBlocks.title: Daughters as guides
narrativeBlocks.body: In the underwater palace, the Water King's daughters are his instruments — but one of them helps the boy instead: she tells him which maiden to choose and how to flee. Escape is won by an ally inside the enemy's house.

narrativeBlocks.title: The bargain's lesson
narrativeBlocks.body: This is the 'rash promise' tale — the thing you don't know you have is always the thing you can't afford to lose. The father's haste is paid by the child; the escape is earned by the one helper inside.

quiz.prompt: What does the merchant promise the Water King?

choices.text: A bride from the king's daughters
Whatever is at home that he doesn't know about — which turns out to be his newborn son

quiz.explanation: The 'unknown thing' clause is the trap — his haste mortgages a child he hasn't met.

quiz.prompt: How does the son escape the underwater kingdom?

choices.text: The Water King's own daughter helps him — guiding his choice and his flight from her father's palace
He holds his breath and swims to the surface
He bargains for a second chance

quiz.explanation: Escape runs through an insider ally — the helper inside the enemy's house.
